newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot resids mixed, low sulphurs pressured.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot resids mixed, low sulphurs pressured.

text.p: U.S. spot fuel oil prices were mixed Monday in lackluster trade, with low sulphur pressured by soft utility demand, while high sulphur was buoyed by recent Mexican buying and steady bunker demand, sources said.

"Demand is not great - temperatures are supposed to be mild all week - but bunkers are holding," said one cash trader, adding the high sulphur market seemed better balanced but hotter weather was needed to get more upside.
In New York Harbor, physical one percent slipped a quarter to $16.25-50 a barrel, with June paper also talked weaker in the $16.30-60 area, traders said.
NYH 0.3 percent high pour notionally eased slightly to about $17 amid little utility interest.
High sulphurs in New York were steady to higher, with 2.2 percent up slightly to the low-$15 level, traders said.
At the U.S. Gulf, prices again were stable, with one percent still at $16.25 and three percent at $14.25-50.
No NYH or USG deals were reported.

New York city gate natgas prices were unchanged at $2.45/mmBtu area, or $15.44 a barrel equivalent. Gas at Henry Hub, the NYMEX delivery point, slipped a few cents to about $2.20/mmBtu, or $13.86 a barrel.
With little improvement in East Coast or Gulf Coast demand expected right into next week, traders said gas and resid should stay on the defensive near-term.
